Its peak combines a learned lexical set (technical/terminological nouns, proper names, code identifiers and word pieces, which reach 0.4-1.3 on their own) with that closing position, which lifts the same word 4-10x over its plain-context value ('hand' 1.70 vs 0.16, 'style' 1.52 vs 0.20, 'art' 2.09 vs 0.45), whereas closed-class function words, punctuation and bare digits rarely reach a quarter of the maximum (most never exceed 0.3 over ~200k scanned tokens) and core everyday vocabulary or merely-predictable content ('the dog wagged its tail', 'the capital of France is Paris') stays at zero.
